clue.text: Closing time of special significance

parts.note: reads like a pub's last orders, but means the moment a whole historic period finishes

explanation.definitionFit: A significant closing moment is the close of a notable period or epoch in history.

clue.text: Principal, except with heartless tutors, acts the goat

parts.note: a principal is the head of a school
but means except, as in 'all but one'

indicators.note: heartless means the inner letters of tutors are cut away, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A headteacher who, apart from dealing with callous tutors, plays the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acts the goat' usually means fools about, but here it is literal: goats ram with their heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Goats ram things with their heads, so acting like a goat is striking with the forehead.

clue.text: Present downfall that's hurting

parts.note: a downfall is someone's end, as in 'drink was his end'
ow is the cry of something that hurts

explanation.surface: A gift brings about a painful collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: To present someone with money or property is to endow them with it; both mean bestow.

clue.text: Gets rid of bad habits and schemes

definitions.meaning: ... are plans or stratagems, as in 'left to his own ...'

explanation.surface: Someone who gives up vices and plots.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices are contrivances or schemes, and to de-vice is jokily to strip away vices.

clue.text: Crank turning, in fact, engrosses one

indicators.note: engrosses means takes in, so the scrambled letters hold the next piece inside
turning means the letters of in fact are turned about into a new order

parts.note: a is one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A crank handle that, as it rotates, takes in a single item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' scrambles IN FACT to FNATIC; 'engrosses' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A crank is an eccentric obsessive, and a fanatic is someone obsessively devoted to a cause.

clue.text: As Daphne's New York speed dig

parts.note: mph, miles per hour, measures speed
to dig something is slang for liking it

explanation.surface: Daphne in New York is speedy and digs things.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Daphne was a nymph who was turned into a laurel tree to escape Apollo.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne was a mythical nymph, so something like her nature is described as resembling a nymph.

clue.text: Have sufficient money for fast approach

definitions.meaning: to stretch to the cost of
to hurry towards someone, as a child might to its mother

explanation.definitionFit: Being able to afford something and dashing up to someone are both senses of the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: Condition of silly-looking root for a southern aspect

parts.note: to root for someone is to cheer them on, to urge or encourage them
a means one, as in 'a dozen'
an aspect is a face, as the face of a building

explanation.surface: A gardener asks about the state of a silly-looking plant root that faces south.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being embarrassed after looking foolish, the state of appearing silly.

clue.text: "Bitmaps for IFE" exposition's rather hot introduction

indicators.note: an exposition sets out the letters afresh, so the quoted phrase is laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A computing explanation of image files proves a fierce start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposition's' rearranges the nonsense quoted phrase BITMAPS FOR IFE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A first experience that is hard and testing is a punishing initiation, literally one under gunfire.

clue.text: Keeps to front of non-passenger car

parts.note: guards means keeps safe
the van is the front, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: Someone sticks to the front of a goods carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: A guard's van is the British railway carriage at the back of a train for the guard, not passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway guard's van is a carriage carrying staff and luggage rather than paying travellers.

clue.text: Divine food provided by hubby? No!

parts.note: a husband is informally one's man
na is a Scots and dialect word for no

explanation.surface: A wife asks whether her husband provided heavenly food, and answers no.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna was the food that fell from heaven to feed the Israelites in the wilderness.

clue.text: Bend round to kiss missile launcher

parts.note: O is round in shape
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter
a bow launches arrows

explanation.surface: Someone stoops to kiss an archer's weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxbow is a U-shaped bend in a river.

clue.text: Film hides truth about assassin

indicators.note: hides means conceals within, so the coat wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a coat is a thin film or layer, as of paint

indicators.note: about signals the letters of truth moved around

explanation.surface: A movie conceals the facts about a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like cinema but is a thin layer; 'about' is the anagram signal on the second word and 'hides' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-throat is a murderer, especially a ruthless killer for hire.

clue.text: Shops for pieces of veal with fresh topping

indicators.note: fresh topping means the word gets a new first letter in place of its old one

parts.note: cutlets are pieces of meat such as veal

explanation.surface: A butcher sells veal cutlets with a new garnish.
explanation.walkthrough: The new first letter is not clued: the solver must find the letter that turns CUTLETS into a word meaning shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlets are retail stores selling goods.

clue.text: New money's top in bureaucratic jargon

parts.note: the euro was then a new currency; with the possessive it gives euro plus S
a peak is the top of something

explanation.surface: Fresh currency reaches a high point in officialdom's language.
explanation.walkthrough: Eurospeak is the jargon of European Union officials.
explanation.definitionFit: The term mocks the dense official language used by EU administrators.

clue.text: Bed covers love to be replaced by one such as 1, 8, 9 and 26

indicators.note: to be replaced by says one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: cloches are glass covers for plants in garden beds
love is zero in tennis, O
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Bedspreads with a heart motif are swapped for something like other phrases in the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' suggests bedroom, but it is a garden bed. The cross-referenced answers are all stock phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: Each cross-referenced answer is a stock, overused expression, which is what a hackneyed phrase is.

clue.text: Controversial issue of lustful King Edward?

parts.note: hot means sexually eager
King Edward is a popular British variety of potato

explanation.surface: A royal scandal about a lecherous King Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a common British potato variety, not just the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic too awkward to handle, passed on quickly, is likened to something too hot to hold.

clue.text: Not quite ticked off, but not left to chance

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by one letter, its first here

parts.note: to tick someone off is to reprimand or censure them

explanation.surface: Someone was nearly told off but nothing was left to luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ensured has been made certain, guaranteed rather than left to fate.

clue.text: Last of beer in port's for cattlemen

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the port's name

parts.note: Dover is an English port; with the possessive it gives Dover plus S

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: The dregs of beer at the harbour are for the herdsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Drovers drive cattle or sheep to market, so they are herdsmen.

clue.text: West's reflective alternative time conductor

parts.note: Mae West was a Hollywood actress; her possessive gives Mae plus S

indicators.note: reflective means mirrored, so the word for alternative is read backwards

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A Western mirror image is another choice of time-keeper for an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished musician, especially an orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Wimp gets the most out of work

parts.note: to milk something is to exploit it fully
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A feeble person exploits a job to the full.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a weak, timid man, a weakling.

clue.text: Pays for utensil and plates supporter

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay for it
a tool is a utensil

explanation.surface: Someone buys a kitchen implement and some dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plates' is rhyming slang: plates of meat = feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A footstool is a low stool on which feet rest, and plates means feet in slang.

clue.text: Browser's all right with one eye

parts.note: OK means all right
a is one
a private eye is a PI, private investigator

explanation.surface: An internet browser is fine with a single eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browser' looks like software, but means an animal that browses on leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest animal that feeds by browsing on leaves.

clue.text: Switching positions at prison officers' centre

indicators.note: centre means the letters sit in the middle of the words prison officers

explanation.surface: Guards change places at the core of a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch has two positions, live and dead, the settings either way.

clue.text: He's very up on basis for calculating interest

definitions.note: the clue reads He is, the answer being a man's name such as Oscar Wilde

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
CAR is compound annual rate, a basis for working out interest

explanation.surface: A man is well versed in how interest is calculated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places one piece above the next in this down clue; the definition is a male name.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar is a man's first name, so it stands for a 'he'.

clue.text: Group with common ancestry dressed alike finally

parts.note: clad means dressed

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of alike

explanation.surface: Relatives wearing matching outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: A clade is a biological group made of one ancestor and all its descendants.

clue.text: Failing to tax office furniture

parts.note: something that fails to tax you is easy
the chair is an office, as in holding the chair of a committee

explanation.surface: Not paying tax on office furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'office furniture' reads as one phrase, but office is the post of chair.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a comfortable armchair, a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Crestfallen?

parts.note: means downcast, but plays on a bird with a crest being unwell

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means deeply disappointed, and parrots have crests, hence the pun.
